habit.lifeForm.value: large strong-growing deciduous climber with aerial roots
habit.lifeForm.basis: RHS plant record: "A large, strong-growing deciduous climber with aerial roots".

habit.heightM.basis: RHS plant record: ultimate height 8 to 12 m, in 5 to 10 years.

habit.parentage.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online: the name covers hybrids between C. radicans and C. grandiflora; 'Mme Galen' was put into commerce in 1889.

stem.youngSurface.value: green, hairless, flushed red-brown in sun
stem.youngSurface.basis: Bean, of the parent C. radicans: "young stems glabrous". The red-brown flush is read from photographs of the cultivar (reference mg-stang-0, mg-stang-1, mg-helbra-1); the shoot of C. radicans in rad-stem-9 is plain green with pale streaks.

stem.winterTwigColour.basis: Ohio State weed guide, of C. radicans: recognised in winter by "straw-colored branches".

stem.oldBark.value: light tan to yellowish brown, peeling in thin strips
stem.oldBark.basis: Missouri Plants describes the older stems of C. radicans as woody with yellowish-brown bark peeling in thin strips (paraphrased: the page could not be checked word for word). University of Connecticut: bark "light tan", "slightly exfoliating on old trunks". An old trunk of C. radicans in reference rad-old-plant is pale tan and twisted, its bark in long flakes.

holdfast.kind.basis: RHS campsis growing guide: "Campsis is a self-clinging climber, using aerial roots along its long stems to grip onto vertical surfaces". Trees and Shrubs Online, of 'Mme Galen': "It is not a climber that can be left to look after itself", so the hold is weak.

holdfast.rows.basis: Ohio State weed guide, of the parent C. radicans: aerial roots "are formed in 2 rows below nodes on the stem". The other parent has few or none (Burras and Griffiths); nothing read describes them on this cultivar.

holdfast.position.value: in a band below each node, on the side against the support
holdfast.position.basis: Ohio State weed guide, of C. radicans: "aerial roots formed in bands below the leaf nodes on woody stems". In reference rad-rootlets the tuft stands just beside and below a node, on the side against the surface.

holdfast.rootletLengthM.basis: Read from a photograph of the parent C. radicans (reference rad-rootlets): a tuft reaches out about one and a half times the width of a stem some 6 mm through. Not measured on this cultivar.

holdfast.rootletsPerRow.basis: How many rootlets are drawn in each of the two rows of a tuft. Nobody has counted; reference rad-rootlets shows a dozen or so in one tuft of C. radicans.

leaf.arrangement.basis: NC State Extension gives the hybrid's leaf arrangement as opposite; Missouri Plants gives those of C. radicans as opposite and odd-pinnate. Every photograph of the cultivar looked at shows them in pairs (reference mg-stang-1).

leaf.division.basis: NC State Extension, of the hybrid: "compound, odd-pinnate, with 7 to 11 leaflets".

leaf.lengthM.basis: Burras and Griffiths, Manual of Climbers and Wall Plants (1994), of the hybrid, as quoted by Discover Life (checked): "Leaves 20-35cm". Burncoose Nurseries gives this cultivar's leaves as up to 30 cm.

leaf.leafletCount.basis: Burras and Griffiths, Manual of Climbers and Wall Plants (1994), of the hybrid, as quoted by Discover Life (checked): pinnae "7-11". Burncoose, of this cultivar: 7 to 11 oval leaflets. NC State: 7 to 11. The RHS record says "up to 15 small leaflets", which no other source repeats. The leaf of the cultivar in reference mg-stang-1 has 11.

leaf.leafletCountUsual.basis: The middle of the published range of 7 to 11; the leaf has an odd number. No source says which is commonest on this cultivar.

leaf.leafletLengthMaxM.basis: Burras and Griffiths, Manual of Climbers and Wall Plants (1994), of the hybrid, as quoted by Discover Life: "pinnae to 8x4.5cm".

leaf.leafletWidthMaxM.basis: Burras and Griffiths, Manual of Climbers and Wall Plants (1994), of the hybrid, as quoted by Discover Life: "pinnae to 8x4.5cm".

leaf.widthShareOfLength.basis: Width of the whole leaf for its length. Oates et al. (HortScience 49: 343-345, 2014, Table 1) measured leaf length and width on four other Campsis: 0.41 for the hybrid 'Kudian', 0.40 for the hybrid 'Chastity', 0.45 for C. grandiflora. 'Madame Galen' was grown in that trial and not measured; a value among its relatives is taken.

leaf.leafletShape.basis: Oates et al. 2014, of the genus: each leaflet ovate with an attenuate apex and a coarsely dentate margin (paraphrased). Bean, of C. radicans: "ovate", ending in "a long, often tail-like point".

leaf.leafletMargin.basis: Oates et al. 2014: a coarsely dentate margin (paraphrased). Burras and Griffiths, of the hybrid: "serrate". Bean, of C. radicans: "coarsely and angularly toothed".

leaf.leafletTeethPerSide.basis: Teeth on each side of a leaflet, the fewest and the most, counted on photographs of the cultivar (reference mg-stang-1: four to seven, uneven in size and spacing, none on the rounded base or the long point; hyb-badduben-1 the same). Floras say only that the teeth are coarse.

leaf.leafletLateralVeinPairs.basis: Flora of China gives 6 or 7 pairs of lateral veins for the parent C. grandiflora (as reported by Wikipedia; the flora itself could not be opened). Taken for the hybrid.

leaf.leafletStalkLengthM.basis: Between the parents: about 0.5 mm in C. radicans, "longer on basal leaflets" (Gentry 1992), and 5 mm in C. grandiflora (Flora of China, as reported). Not measured on this cultivar.

leaf.stalkShareOfLength.basis: The leaf stalk below the first pair of leaflets, as a share of the leaf, measured on reference mg-stang-1 (about a tenth). No source measures it.

leaf.rachis.basis: Missouri Plants, of C. radicans: rachis with a narrow groove on its upper side (paraphrased). Burras and Griffiths, of the hybrid: "rachis pilose". In reference mg-stang-1 the axis of a young leaf is flushed red-purple.

leaf.surfaceAbove.basis: NC State Extension, of the hybrid: shiny green above (paraphrased). Burncoose, of this cultivar: dark green. The photographs (mg-stang-1, hyb-badduben-1) show a mid green, darker in shade, the blade puckered between sunk veins.

leaf.surfaceBeneath.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online: 'Mme Galen' "resembles C. radicans in having the leaves downy beneath". Burras and Griffiths: "light pubescent above and on veins beneath". (NC State calls the hybrid hairless beneath; the account of the cultivar is followed.)

leaf.colourYoung.basis: How the unfolding leaf is coloured in the drawing. No source read describes the young foliage of this cultivar; the young leaves in reference mg-stang-0 and mg-stang-1 are green edged and veined with red-brown.

leaf.autumnColour.basis: University of Connecticut, of C. radicans: "fall color is poor", the foliage "yellow-green". Ohio State: "Leaves turn yellowish before dropping off in autumn".

inflorescence.type.basis: Trees and Shrubs Online: 'Mme Galen' resembles "the other parent in its lax truss" (C. grandiflora). Burncoose: terminal clusters of 6 to 12 flowers. In photographs of the cultivar (reference mg-ubc, mg-huntington) a truss is a loose head at the end of an arching shoot, its open flowers facing out among many buds.

inflorescence.position.value: at the end of a shoot of the current year
inflorescence.position.basis: Bean, of C. radicans: "in a cluster at the end of the current season's growth".

inflorescence.flowerCount.basis: Burncoose Nurseries gives this cultivar's flowers as in terminal clusters of 6 to 12 (paraphrased). The RHS A-Z Encyclopedia, as cited by Wikipedia: loose clusters of 6 to 12. Bean, of C. radicans: four to twelve; University of Connecticut: "4 to a dozen". Photographs of the cultivar in flower (reference mg-huntington) show a dozen or more buds on one truss with few open at once; the published count is kept.

inflorescence.branching.value: branches in opposite pairs, the lower three-flowered, the upper one-flowered
inflorescence.branching.basis: How the truss is drawn. That a panicle of the family is built of opposite cymes is general knowledge of Bignoniaceae and was not read in a description of this plant.

inflorescence.lengthM.basis: What RenderFlower.lengthM measures for this taxon, and what the model of the truss is authored to: the length of a truss from where it leaves the shoot to the mouths of its end flowers. The same range as organs.racemeLengthM in the growth model, where its basis is given. No source measures a truss of this cultivar.

inflorescence.axisLengthM.basis: The stalk and axis of the truss. Flora of China gives 15 to 20 cm for the parent C. grandiflora (as reported by Wikipedia; the flora itself could not be opened). In photographs of the cultivar the flowers stand crowded on the last part of it (reference mg-huntington), which is how it is drawn.

inflorescence.flowerStalkLengthM.basis: Missouri Plants, of C. radicans: pedicels to 1.7 cm long (paraphrased). Not given for the hybrid.

inflorescence.opening.value: a few flowers at a time, from the base of the truss
inflorescence.opening.basis: University of Michigan climbers database, of C. radicans: "Not all flowers bloom at once". That the lowest open first is how the truss is drawn and was not read anywhere.

flower.shape.value: trumpet: a tube narrow at the base, widening to a flared limb of five rounded lobes
flower.shape.basis: Burras and Griffiths, Manual of Climbers and Wall Plants (1994), of the hybrid, as quoted by Discover Life: "corolla tubular-campanulate ... base narrow, widening to 3 cm across at throat". Bean, of C. radicans: "five broad, short, rounded lobes".

flower.lengthM.basis: The RHS A-Z Encyclopedia of Garden Plants, as cited by Wikipedia, of this cultivar: flowers up to 8 cm long. NC State: about 3 inches long. (Both paraphrased.)

flower.tubeLengthM.basis: Burras and Griffiths, Manual of Climbers and Wall Plants (1994), of the hybrid, as quoted by Discover Life: "tube to 6.5cm".

flower.throatWidthM.basis: Burras and Griffiths, Manual of Climbers and Wall Plants (1994), of the hybrid, as quoted by Discover Life: "widening to 3 cm across at throat".

flower.tubeBaseWidthM.basis: Width of the tube where it leaves the calyx. Oates et al. 2014 measured the narrow end of the corolla at 6 mm on the hybrid 'Kudian' and 10 mm on 'Chastity'; 'Madame Galen' was not measured.

flower.limbWidthM.basis: Burras and Griffiths, Manual of Climbers and Wall Plants (1994), of the hybrid, as quoted by Discover Life: "limb to 6.5 cm diameter". RHS plant record, of this cultivar: "Flowers tubular, reddish-orange, with limb to 8cm in width". Havlis: "The flowers are huge, 7-9 cm wide".

flower.lobeCount.basis: Bean, of C. radicans: "five broad, short, rounded lobes". Every photograph of the cultivar shows five.

flower.lobeLengthM.basis: Burras and Griffiths, Manual of Climbers and Wall Plants (1994), of the hybrid, as quoted by Discover Life: "lobes to 3.8 x 2.4 cm". Read as 2.4 cm long and 3.8 cm wide, which is what a limb 6.5 cm across with five broad lobes allows; the source does not say which figure is which.

flower.lobeWidthM.basis: Burras and Griffiths, Manual of Climbers and Wall Plants (1994), of the hybrid, as quoted by Discover Life: "lobes to 3.8 x 2.4 cm". See flower.lobeLengthM.

flower.symmetry.value: slightly two-lipped: the two upper lobes a little smaller
flower.symmetry.basis: Missouri Plants describes the corolla of C. radicans as somewhat zygomorphic, the two upper lobes a little smaller (paraphrased).

flower.colourLimb.basis: Burncoose, of this cultivar: "Salmon-red trumpets". NC State: cantaloupe-orange to salmon-red (paraphrased). RHS plant record: "reddish-orange". Havlis: "orange red with apricot orange throat". Photographs of the cultivar (mg-ubc, mg-huntington, mg-vlasenko-a) show a deep salmon-red to orange-red limb.

flower.colourTubeOutside.basis: Burras and Griffiths, Manual of Climbers and Wall Plants (1994), of the hybrid, as quoted by Discover Life: "orange outside, scarlet inside".

flower.colourThroat.basis: Havlis nursery catalogue, of this cultivar: "orange red with apricot orange throat". The fine red lines running into the throat are seen in photographs of the hybrid (reference hyb-madrid-1, mg-vlasenko-a); Oates et al. 2014 describe red striping on the hybrid 'Chastity'.

flower.calyxLengthM.basis: Between the parents: 15 to 22 mm in C. radicans (Missouri Plants; Bean gives about 5/8 in.), about 30 mm in C. grandiflora (Bean: 1 1/4 in.). Not measured on this cultivar.

flower.calyxLobing.basis: How far the calyx is cut into its five teeth, as a share of its length. Between the parents: short triangular teeth in C. radicans (Bean), cut to the middle in C. grandiflora (Bean: lobes 1/2 in. of 1 1/4 in.).

flower.calyxColour.value: yellow-green, ochre to orange at the teeth
flower.calyxColour.basis: Read from photographs of the cultivar and the hybrid: green to yellow-green calyces in reference mg-huntington and hyb-hockenheim-2018, ochre and orange-tinged in mg-ubc, reddish in mg-helbra-2. No source read gives the colour on this cultivar.

flower.stamenCount.basis: Missouri Plants, of C. radicans: stamens 4, included (paraphrased). Gentry 1992: didynamous and included, the anthers held not far below the tube mouth (paraphrased). Yellow anthers show at the mouth in reference hyb-madrid-1.

flower.antherLengthM.basis: Gentry 1992, of C. radicans: anther thecae 3 to 4 mm long.

flower.styleLengthM.basis: Missouri Plants, of C. radicans: style 4.8 cm long, the stigma flattened (paraphrased).

fruit.type.basis: Gentry 1992, of C. radicans: capsule with "valves smooth and subwoody". NC State, of the hybrid: "bean-like seed pod".

fruit.shape.value: spindle-shaped, stalked, pointed, ridged along the two seams
fruit.shape.basis: Bean, of C. radicans: pod "spindle-shaped, stout". Gentry: stalked, acuminate at the apex (paraphrased). The pods of the hybrid in reference hyb-fruit-1 are spindle-shaped, ridged along their seams and between them, with the dried black calyx standing as a star at the top.

fruit.lengthM.basis: From the parents: C. radicans "5 in. long" (Bean), C. grandiflora 7 to 12 cm (Flora of China, as reported by Wikipedia). The pods of the hybrid in reference hyb-fruit-1 are about a hand long. No source measures a pod of this cultivar.

fruit.widthM.basis: Bean, of C. radicans: pod "3/4 in. wide in the middle". Not given for the hybrid.

fruit.colourUnripe.basis: University of Connecticut, of C. radicans: capsules "change from green to tan". Reference hyb-fruit-1 shows the hybrid's pods a pale grey-green in late October.

fruit.colourRipe.basis: Missouri Plants, of C. radicans: valves tan to brown when ripe (paraphrased). University of Connecticut: "change from green to tan". Reference rad-january-1: split pods a pale tan in January.

fruit.setInBritain.basis: Bean, of C. radicans: pods form "Very rarely, but sometimes after unusually hot summers".

fruit.seed.basis: Bean, of C. radicans: pods "full of flattened seeds with silvery transparent wings".

leaf.leafletWidestAt.basis: Where along a leaflet it is widest, base to tip, measured on the leaflets of reference mg-stang-1 (about a third of the way up; the base broad and rounded, the tip drawn out).

leaf.leafletForwardDeg.basis: How far forward of square to the leaf's axis the side leaflets point, from the lowest pair to the last, measured on reference mg-stang-1 (the lowest pairs nearly square, the upper ones leaning towards the tip).

leaf.posture.value: on a wall, turned out and hanging face out, the end leaflet lowest; on a shoot in the open, held flatter and drooping
leaf.posture.basis: Read from photographs: reference hyb-badduben-1 (the hybrid on a house wall: every leaf hangs face out, tip down, whichever way its stem runs), mg-ubc and mg-stang-2 (leaves on free shoots spread and droop from their axes).

leaf.faceRiseDeg.basis: How far above level the upper face of a leaf looks, its stem lying against an upright surface: reference hyb-badduben-1, where the leaves face out from the wall, a little up.

leaf.faceRiseOpenDeg.basis: The same on a shoot out in the open: reference mg-ubc and mg-helbra-1, where the leaves are held more to the sky and droop from their axes.

leaf.bladeTurnDeg.basis: How far a leaf is turned about its face from tip-straight-down: in reference hyb-badduben-1 the leaves hang within about thirty degrees either way of plumb.
